clue.text: Sanctuary unknown in a degraded area

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the phrase for a run-down district

parts.note: a slum is a squalid, run-down area
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A refuge from the unknown found in a run-down neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or refuge granted to someone fleeing danger, a synonym of sanctuary.

clue.text: Setter's visas having insuperable problems

parts.note: the setter says 'I'm', so Setter's (setter is) gives IM
passes are permits or visas allowing entry

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler's travel permits are running into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadlocks with no way forward are problems that cannot be overcome.

clue.text: Prepared that fellow with money to support US lawyer

indicators.note: in a down clue the lawyer sits on top of the other pieces, which hold it up from below

parts.note: Att. abbreviates attorney, the American word for a lawyer
he refers to a male person
the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A man with funds is set to back an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' works because this is a down clue: HE and READY are written below ATT, so they support it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something poised for immediate use, i.e. prepared.

clue.text: Confusion over study about entrance to harbour (place a little way out to sea)

definitions.text: place a little way out to sea

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the rest

parts.note: pie (or pi) is printers' jumbled type, so confusion

indicators.note: about means the study word is wrapped around the letter that follows

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Mixed-up research concerning the way into a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance to harbour' looks like the definition but it only supplies H; the definition is the bracketed phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaward end of a pier, or a jetty, juts slightly out into the water.

clue.text: River valley starts to widen after downpour initially

indicators.note: the starts of the following words give their opening letters

explanation.surface: A river valley begins to broaden after an initial cloudburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' reads as another indicator, but it is the fourth word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry North African or Arabian valley that fills with water after rain.

clue.text: I'm … I'm afraid to pick up sausage

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up means lifting, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret, like I'm afraid

explanation.surface: Someone stammering an apology while collecting a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: The first I'm stands for itself; the second I'm goes with afraid to give ALAS. The 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spicy, cured Italian sausage.

clue.text: Ridiculous oven set up in university city

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the university-plus-city pair

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a kiln is an oven for firing pottery

explanation.surface: An absurd kiln installed in a college town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' signals reversal because in a down clue the word is written upwards. Ely is a small English cathedral city near Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improbable, as in a far-fetched story, can be called ridiculous.

clue.text: Object very much encountered in Government around end of March

indicators.note: around means the whole string of pieces surrounds the final letter of the month

parts.note: so means very much, as in so tired
met means encountered

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Something greatly resisted by the authorities at the close of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps SOMETING around H, the last letter of March, giving SOMET-H-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: An unspecified item or entity, a thing, is an object.

clue.text: Leave, following being involved in error

indicators.note: the abbreviation becomes part of the error word, inserted within it

parts.note: a goof is a blunder
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. 6f.

explanation.surface: Departing after being caught up in a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to depart or exit, so to leave.

clue.text: Range currently stocked? At a subsequent time, rather

definitions.note: the definition is an adverb phrase, matching the answer

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of cooking range
goods in stock are in

explanation.surface: A shop asks whether its stoves are now in stock, and promises more later.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a heavy British kitchen stove brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Another time, later on, a second occasion: the adverb means once more, at a later time.

clue.text: Product of cows from meadow yonder? Not entirely

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is taken without its final letter

parts.note: yonder means over there

explanation.surface: Something cows produce, seen in a field over there, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide from cattle is tanned into this material, so it comes from cows.

clue.text: Almost fail to involve European city in work on paper

indicators.note: involve means the shortened word takes the city inside it
almost means all but the last letter

parts.note: to fail to do something is to omit it
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: Nearly forgetting to include a Baltic capital in a paper exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fail' is a verb here, as in failing to mention something; 'Almost' drops its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese craft of folding is literally work done with paper.

clue.text: Title for man giving nowt ultimately away?

definitions.text: Title for man giving nowt ultimately away?

indicators.note: giving it away means the letter is removed from the title

parts.note: Mister is the title for a man

indicators.note: ultimately means the word's final letter

explanation.surface: A name for a fellow who never gives anything away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving ... away' removes T, the last letter of nowt, from MISTER. Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a man who gives nowt (Northern English for nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted hoarder is someone who parts with nothing.

clue.text: Fighter plane brought in faulty, not initially operational

indicators.note: brought in means the plane's letter is put inside the shortened word
not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: defective means faulty
F designates a fighter aircraft, as in F-16

explanation.surface: A combat jet delivered broken, not working at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' turns DEFECTIVE into EFECTIVE; F goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in force and working, such as a law from a set date, is operational.

clue.text: Appalachian holiday venue affected and reduced under pressure?

parts.note: camp means exaggerated or affected in manner
grain that is ground has been crushed small under a millstone's pressure

explanation.surface: A mountain resort that has been made pretentious and cut down by stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under pressure' is not a separate P; it describes how grinding reduces something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is American usage for a camping site, so Appalachian marks it as a US holiday spot.

clue.text: Dr Rory, a Scotsman, could be working here

definitions.text: Dr Rory, a Scotsman, could be working here

indicators.note: the letters, if working differently, could be rearranged into a place name

explanation.surface: A Scottish doctor might have his practice in this region.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross and Cromarty is a former county in the Scottish Highlands, so a Scots doctor could indeed practise there.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic Highland county is a place where a Scottish physician might work.

clue.text: Bawdy writer redrafted serial, penning a book

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the rearranged letters surround the pair
a redrafted text is rewritten, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ribald author rewrote his serial, adding a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redrafted' turns SERIAL into RELAIS, which pens A and B after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The French author of Gargantua and Pantagruel is famed for coarse, earthy comedy.

clue.text: Others work squeezing Edward's organ part

indicators.note: squeezing means holding tightly, so the name sits inside the other letters

parts.note: the rest are the others
Ed is short for Edward; the 's is part of the surface
op. abbreviates opus, a work

explanation.surface: Other people's work pressed into Edward's instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of reed pipes controlled by one knob is a component of a pipe organ.

clue.text: Nasal problem? Suggestion is provided about one after runs

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the letter for runs

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: about means the hint word goes around the numeral

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor's hint about a runny nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' is a link. 'runs' suggests a runny nose but supplies only R.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the nose's mucous membrane is a nasal complaint.

clue.text: Mixture of bleach and lye gives you stomach pain

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Drinking a cocktail of household chemicals upsets your stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a pain in the belly, or colic, is a stomach ache.

clue.text: Lively activity seen around a new Scots town

indicators.note: around means the activity word surrounds the two letters

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or spree

explanation.surface: Merriment breaks out around a newly founded Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanark is a town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Island location where herd's heard?

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud rather than written

parts.note: a herd's, possessively, belongs to the cows

explanation.surface: Where on an island can the cattle be heard?
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a sailing town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Isle of Wight is a place on an island.

clue.text: German linguist forbidding using repeated letter at the end

parts.note: grim means forbidding or stern

parts.words: using repeated letter at the end
parts.note: the last letter of the stern word is used again, adding a second copy at the end

explanation.surface: A stern German language scholar who doubles letters at the end of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Grimm, of the fairy tales, formulated Grimm's Law of sound change in Germanic languages.

clue.text: Predominantly with some dampness but no current

indicators.note: but no means the following element is left out

parts.note: moistly means in a damp way
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A weather report: largely damp, with no flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: For the most part, or mainly, means predominantly.

clue.text: Wooden weapon with pine front

parts.note: to pine for is to long for
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A weapon made from pine wood, with a front end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' is the verb (yearn), not the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The English yew bow was a weapon made of wood.

clue.text: Lad accepting kiss with an indifferent sound?

indicators.note: accepting means the lad's word takes the letter in

parts.note: a boy is a lad
X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: A boy getting a kiss responds with a shrug of a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio described as boxy is muffled and hollow, so of mediocre quality.

clue.text: Keeps absorbing Independent news items

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: stores means keeps

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper hangs on to its reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists call the articles they file pieces or reports, so news items.

clue.text: One place for matches involving Rangers primarily?

definitions.text: One place for matches involving Rangers primarily?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: involving means the letter is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: a matchbox is a box, a place to keep matches

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A venue whose fixtures chiefly feature Rangers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibrox is the Glasgow stadium of Rangers football club, so the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A football ground hosts fixtures, and this one is home to a Glasgow club.

clue.text: Bird to show affection in two ways

parts.note: to spoon is to kiss and cuddle
the same idea expressed a second way: to bill, as in bill and coo

explanation.surface: A bird that has two ways of being amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird with a flat, broad beak is one of the ibis family.
